research_question: When the required operator schema is absent from the supplied ontology and is not explicitly stated as target preconditions/effects, can an engine infer the unique reusable operator from structured positive and negative transition examples?
claim_boundary: formal operator induction inside a frozen typed symbolic hypothesis space; not raw-language parsing, world-knowledge invention, or open-ended semantic synthesis

visible_input.parameters: ordered visible variable names with declared types
visible_input.supplied_primitive_ontology: known operator schemas intentionally excluding the hidden target semantic signature
visible_input.positive_examples: at least 2 state transitions, each with parameter binding, before state, and after state
visible_input.negative_examples: one per hidden precondition, each with binding and unchanged before/after state
visible_input.heldout_target: new entity binding plus before state only; heldout after state hidden from both engines

hypothesis_space.atom_templates: all and only type-compatible predicate applications to visible parameter variables

output_schema.parameters: exact ordered visible parameter-variable list; grammar-constrained, not a scored free-text decision
output_schema.preconditions: unordered set of visible typed atom templates
output_schema.add_effects: unordered set of visible typed atom templates
output_schema.delete_effects: unordered set containing exactly one visible typed atom template

transition_semantics.applicable: every precondition atom instantiated under the example binding exists in before state
transition_semantics.apply: after = (before - instantiated delete_effects) union instantiated add_effects
transition_semantics.positive_consistency: operator is applicable and computed after equals visible after exactly
transition_semantics.negative_consistency: visible after equals before and operator is not applicable because at least one instantiated precondition is absent

identifiability_gate.hidden_oracle: the unique semantic signature from an independent brute-force evaluator

heldout_target_gate.scoring: proposal must equal the unique semantic signature and reproduce hidden heldout after under the formal transition semantics

generator_design_constraints.negative_examples: one omission example for each hidden precondition
generator_design_constraints.positive_noise_rule: positive examples contain different non-common noise atoms so noise cannot become a spurious common precondition
generator_design_constraints.negative_omission_rule: each negative contains all hidden preconditions except exactly one, preventing every proper hidden-precondition subset from satisfying all negatives

qwen.grammar_policy: JSON structure, exact visible parameter list, and typed visible atom vocabulary are constrained; semantic atom selection remains free inside the same frozen hypothesis space
